basis: Neurodevelopmental disability defines syndrome; cardiac defects, strabismus/ptosis and urethral hypospadias each have HPO frequencies of 30-79%.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a urethral malformation, annotated 30-79%; urethra belongs to the renal axis. Ambiguous genitalia alone would not qualify.

basis: Hypothalamic-pituitary and neurodevelopmental dysfunction define PWS; scoliosis occurs in 150/180 (~83%) and strabismus in 30-79%.

decisions.ocular: involved: persistent strabismus causes ocular alignment dysfunction and is annotated frequent (30-79%).

basis: Skin ulceration, osteolysis and oligodontia are defining features; keratitis caused visual impairment or blindness in 3/5 siblings (~60%).

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oligodontia is explicitly part of the defining syndrome and annotated 80-99%; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.

basis: Joint contractures, skeletal fusions and congenital cutaneous pterygia define this multiple-pterygium syndrome.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: the named pterygia are congenital skin webs forming a defining structural component of the syndrome.

basis: Cobalamin processing defect with megaloblastic marrow disease (80-99%); intellectual disability and movement impairment occur in 80-99%.

decisions.haematologic: primary: intrinsic megaloblastic marrow disease, annotated 80-99%, makes this a blood/marrow disorder as well as an inborn metabolic disorder.

basis: Combined immunodeficiency intrinsically affects lymphocytes, with T-cell depletion in 1/1; lymphoma is separately diagnosed and hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: intrinsic lymphocyte depletion and dysfunction constitute blood-cell disease; pancytopenia is also reported in 1/1 but need not establish the axis alone.

basis: Cerebellar ataxia and peripheral neuropathy define disease; distal muscle wasting in 1/1 reflects denervation, without evidence of direct muscle disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: wasting and weakness are downstream effects of neuropathy; direct skeletal-muscle pathology or common structural skeletal injury is not established.

basis: Retinal vascular leakage injures the macula; the underlying diabetes is a separate disease, not an additional organ affected by macular edema.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: macular edema is a localized retinal complication; underlying diabetes and metabolic ancestry do not make it an intrinsic metabolic disorder.

basis: Metabolic enzyme deficiency; cataracts in 3/4. Neurodevelopmental/CNS impairment is a common core feature (>30%); hepatic, cardiac and pancreatic injury each 1/4.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental impairment with CNS abnormalities is a common syndrome manifestation (estimated >30%); supplied HPO entries lack a precise frequency.

basis: Defining skeletal dysplasia with progressive kyphoscoliosis; respiratory insufficiency in 1/2 reflects thoracic restriction without established direct pulmonary injury.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory insufficiency (1/2) can result from skeletal thoracic restriction; the supplied evidence does not establish direct lung or airway damage.
